# Marketing Research and Application Candidates — 2026-09-30

## Executive summary

The research agents have identified a focused market hypothesis for Averion Compass: help lean property operations teams carry inspection findings through assigned repair, verification, and a documented ready decision. Competitors already offer inspections, maintenance, and turns, so the opportunity depends on proving a better handoff for a specific operator—not on feature breadth or an NSPIRE compliance claim.

There are researched prospect candidates, but no confirmed applicant, design partner, pilot, or customer. Candidate evidence supports fit for discovery only. No outreach has been approved or sent. The latest scheduled marketing-agent cycles generated drafts, not fresh research, and all six outputs remained in review after QA flags.

## What the agents found

### Market and product

- Inspection-to-repair follow-through is the strongest workflow hypothesis: ownership, evidence, status, and the ready decision can be split across forms, work queues, spreadsheets, and messages.
- Lean multifamily teams, especially affordable or mixed-income operators and conventional operators in roughly the 50–500 unit range, are a segment to test—not a validated ICP.
- Existing platforms already market inspections, maintenance, and unit turns. A focused companion workflow may be easier to test than a system replacement, but buyers may reject another login or source of truth.
- Review sites offer interview prompts about records/evidence, handoffs, configuration, and mobile field work. These are anecdotal signals, not prevalence data.
- HUD/NSPIRE timing creates a timely discovery topic for affordable housing. It does not establish demand or support claims that Compass is compliant, HUD-approved, or automates compliance.
- Product ideas worth auditing: direct finding-to-work conversion with ownership/due date; verified closeout with evidence; escalation rules; customer template governance; and inspection comparison/history. Some may already exist beyond what the reviewed notes establish.

### Commercial and operational readiness

- The lead sprint produced a company-level qualification queue. The strongest numeric fits were NYCHA (78) and Chicago Housing Authority (71); HACLA and FPI scored 64. These scores are triage signals, not validated buying intent.
- WinnResidential has a separate contact-path review: official general business routes and a plausible affordable-housing operations/maintenance routing request were identified. The appropriate region, workflow owner, active pain, baseline, and pilot path remain unknown.
- The September 30 daily brief observed six scheduled runs: three LinkedIn drafts, two pilot-intake drafts, and one pricing-hypothesis draft. All six were `needs-review`; four items awaited approval, ten were blocked, one queued. The lead queue showed 3 approved / 14 pending, with no outcomes recorded.
- Draft QA found missing approved CTAs, an unsupported unit-turn claim, and unverified pricing/implementation language. No post, outreach, website change, demo, or pilot result was verified.
- Execution records live in the active renamed checkout, while the durable vault is a reporting copy. Those sources are not reconciled, so old vault database/dashboard counts should not be used as current queue state.

## Application candidates

If “application” means organizations that might apply Compass to a real workflow, the current candidates are discovery prospects only:

| Candidate | Why it merits discovery | Main gap / route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FPI Management | Affordable and conventional operator; public materials describe maintenance, resident relations, and owner reporting. Potentially more approachable than a large public authority. | Validate the exact inspection-to-repair workflow, regional owner, volume, and budget path. No contact path reviewed here. |
| WinnResidential | Affordable/multifamily and rehabilitation context; public evidence supports operations and maintenance relevance. A general business contact route has been reviewed. | Identify a bounded region/property group and route to an operations/maintenance owner; confirm a real pain and baseline. |
| NYCHA | Highest qualification score; public inspection, repair follow-up, and procurement signals. | Large public procurement environment; confirm an appropriate narrow workflow and buying authority. Longer path likely. |
| Chicago Housing Authority | Strong qualification score and published property-management contracts covering maintenance, repairs, and inspections. | Confirm whether CHA or a contracted property manager owns the target workflow and can sponsor a pilot. |
| HACLA | Published inspection and asset-management evidence. | Validate operating volume and buying authority before investing in outreach. |

Recommendation: begin with one non-government operator (FPI or WinnResidential) and one public-sector comparator (Chicago or NYCHA) for company-level discovery research. Winn has the clearest reviewed business routing path; FPI may be a more approachable operator hypothesis. This is a proposed research sequence, not an outreach authorization or a conclusion that either is a qualified customer.

## Next steps

1. Reconcile the scheduled checkout and vault reporting source so daily reporting reads the same execution state.
2. Triage the 4 awaiting-approval and 10 blocked items in the active control room; retire stale CovePM artifacts before review.
3. Audit the current Compass release for finding-to-work conversion, verified closeout, comparison/history, templates, reminders, and the proposed pilot workflow. Record exact behavior and capability evidence.
4. Produce two focused company-level research briefs (suggested: WinnResidential plus FPI, or one of those plus CHA/NYCHA). Confirm the workflow owner, current process, volume, system of record, buying path, and candidate baseline.
5. Conduct 8–12 operator discovery conversations across affordable/mixed-income and conventional multifamily. Ask for a walkthrough of a recent inspection that generated repair work; look for repeated pain and a budget owner.
6. Only if product fit and operator interest are established, define a small pilot: properties, roles, duration, data boundaries, baseline, success measures, and commercial terms. Seek explicit approval before contacting any recipient or sending a message.
7. Repair content QA inputs before retrying drafts: use supported Compass wording, an approved CTA, source links, and no pricing or implementation assertion without evidence.

## Limits

This report summarizes the dated research and daily brief present in the durable vault as of September 30, 2026. Prospect scores are based on supplied company-level evidence and do not demonstrate interest, need, procurement eligibility, or willingness to pilot.
